name: Kalshi BTC market update velocity
description: How fast the bound Kalshi market is updating. quote_updates_1s and quote_updates_10s count admitted quote updates on either outcome of the market over the trailing one and ten seconds; trades_1s and trades_10s count admitted trades over the same windows; midpoint_changes_10s counts the admitted quote updates in the last ten seconds whose affirmative midpoint differed from the previously admitted one, so a stream of requoted-but-unchanged books is visible as motion without price discovery. velocity_ratio compares the ten-second quote rate with the trailing baseline rate over baseline_window_ms of observed lane time, capped at five minutes (a research default): it is (quote_updates_10s / 10 s) divided by (baseline_quote_updates / baseline window), formed as a single exact ratio so nothing rounds before the comparison. One means the market is updating at its own recent average. Before any baseline exists the ratio has no denominator, so velocity_ratio_present is false and velocity_ratio is left at zero rather than fabricated - the same presence idiom book_resilience uses for recovery_ms. Every count is a fold over admitted event times, never a wall clock, so a replay of the same admissions reproduces every number. Not ready until ten seconds of lane time have been observed since this generation's first admitted event, so the ten-second counts are complete rather than partial; while warming the instance-status reason is market_contract_warming_up. The identity is market-scoped: it fails closed while the venue is unbound, the market contract is still warming, or the affirmative quote is missing, stale or crossed, and it publishes no value rather than a stale one. Its rolling history is per generation and is cleared at the market roll, so a reading never mixes two contracts (ruling E51, spec C3 §2). The history is rolling market-relative state and is deliberately not checkpointed: it re-warms after a restart. All arithmetic is exact decimal and causal - every published number is a fold over admitted events at or before the decision instant. Decimal outputs are rounded to eight places using round-half-to-even.
